```
   319→                try:
   320→                    from source.utils import download_file as download_file
   321→                    local_filename = Path(predecessor_output_url).name
   322→                    local_download_path = segment_processing_dir / f"svi_predecessor_{segment_idx:02d}_{local_filename}"
   323→
   324→                    if not local_download_path.exists():
   325→                        download_file(predecessor_output_url, segment_processing_dir, local_download_path.name)
   326→                        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: Downloaded predecessor video to {local_download_path}")
   327→                    else:
   328→                        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: Predecessor video already exists at {local_download_path}")
   329→
   330→                    predecessor_video_path = str(local_download_path)
   331→                except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as e_dl:
   332→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: Failed to download predecessor video: {e_dl}")
   333→                    predecessor_video_path = None
   334→
   335→            # SVI CRITICAL: Extract only the last ~9 frames (5 + overlap_size) from predecessor
   336→            # WGP uses prefix_video[:, -(5 + overlap_size):] to create overlapped_latents,
   337→            # but then prepends the ENTIRE prefix_video to output. By extracting only the
   338→            # last frames ourselves, we limit what gets prepended.
   339→            if predecessor_video_path and Path(predecessor_video_path).exists():
   340→                from source.media.video import (
   341→                    get_video_frame_count_and_fps as get_video_frame_count_and_fps,
   342→                    extract_frame_range_to_video as extract_frame_range_to_video
   343→                )
   344→
   345→                # Get predecessor video frame count
   346→                pred_frames, pred_fps = get_video_frame_count_and_fps(predecessor_video_path)
   347→                if pred_frames and pred_frames > 0:
   348→                    # IMPORTANT GROUND TRUTH:
   349→                    # Wan2GP SVI continuation uses the last (5 + overlap_size) frames of prefix_video
   350→                    # to build `overlapped_latents`. The extra 5 frames are *model context*; the
   351→                    # overlap_size (4) is the actual stitch overlap we keep in the final segment.
   352→                    #
   353→                    # So we intentionally extract MORE than 4 frames here (usually 9), but after WGP
   354→                    # generation we trim the output so only the last 4 prefix frames remain as the
   355→                    # overlap with the previous segment.
   356→                    prefix_min_context = 5
   357→                    overlap_size = 4  # SVI_STITCH_OVERLAP (pixel-frame overlap)
   358→                    frames_needed = prefix_min_context + overlap_size  # 9 frames total
   359→                    start_frame = max(0, int(pred_frames) - frames_needed)
   360→
   361→                    # GROUND TRUTH LOG: Predecessor video analysis
   362→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: ========== PREDECESSOR ANALYSIS ==========")
   363→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: Predecessor video: {predecessor_video_path}")
   364→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: Predecessor total frames: {pred_frames}")
   365→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: prefix_min_context={prefix_min_context}, overlap_size={overlap_size} => frames_needed={frames_needed}")
   366→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: Extracting frames [{start_frame}:{pred_frames}] (last {frames_needed} frames)")
   367→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: Frame range breakdown:")
   368→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}:   - Frames 0-{start_frame-1}: Will be DISCARDED (not needed)")
   369→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}:   - Frames {start_frame}-{pred_frames-1}: Will be EXTRACTED (last {frames_needed} frames)")
   370→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}:   - Last 4 frames [{pred_frames-4}:{pred_frames-1}]: OVERLAP frames for stitching")
   371→
   372→                    trimmed_prefix_filename = f"svi_prefix_{segment_idx:02d}_last{frames_needed}frames_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}.mp4"
   373→                    trimmed_prefix_path = segment_processing_dir / trimmed_prefix_filename
   374→
   375→                    try:
   376→                        trimmed_result = extract_frame_range_to_video(
   377→                            input_video_path=predecessor_video_path,
   378→                            output_video_path=str(trimmed_prefix_path),
   379→                            start_frame=start_frame,
   380→                            end_frame=None,  # To end
   381→                            fps=float(pred_fps) if pred_fps and pred_fps > 0 else 16.0)
   382→                        # Verify extracted prefix video
   383→                        prefix_frames, prefix_fps = get_video_frame_count_and_fps(trimmed_result)
   384→                        svi_predecessor_video_for_source = str(trimmed_result)
   385→                        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: Extracted prefix video: {prefix_frames} frames (expected: {frames_needed})")
   386→                        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: Prefix video path: {trimmed_result}")
   387→                        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: This prefix will be passed to WGP as video_source")
   388→                        if prefix_frames != frames_needed:
   389→                            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Seg {segment_idx}: WARNING: Extracted {prefix_frames} frames, expected {frames_needed}")
   390→                    except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as e_trim:
   391→                        # Fallback: use full video if extraction failed
   392→                        svi_predecessor_video_for_source = predecessor_video_path
   393→                        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: WARNING - Failed to extract last frames ({e_trim}), using full predecessor video")
   394→                else:
   395→                    # Fallback: use full video if we can't get frame count
   396→                    svi_predecessor_video_for_source = predecessor_video_path
   397→                    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: Could not get predecessor frame count, using full video")
   398→
   399→                # Still extract last frame for image_refs (anchor reference)
   400→                start_ref_path = extract_last_frame_as_image(
   401→                    predecessor_video_path,
   402→                    segment_processing_dir,
   403→                    task_id
   404→                )
   405→                task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: Extracted last frame as anchor start_ref: {start_ref_path}")
   406→            else:
   407→                task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: ERROR - Predecessor video not available at {predecessor_video_path}")
   408→
   409→        # For SVI, end_ref is the target image from input array
   410→        target_end_idx = segment_idx + 1 if segment_idx > 0 else 1
   411→        if svi_predecessor_video_url and segment_idx == 0:
   412→            target_end_idx = 1 if len(orchestrator_images) > 1 else 0
   413→
   414→        if len(orchestrator_images) > target_end_idx:
   415→            end_ref_path = orchestrator_images[target_end_idx]
   416→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: end_ref from input_images[{target_end_idx}]: {end_ref_path}")
   417→        elif len(orchestrator_images) > 0:
   418→            end_ref_path = orchestrator_images[-1]
   419→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: end_ref fallback to last input image: {end_ref_path}")
   420→
   421→    # =============================================================================
   422→    # SVI MODE: First segment uses input images normally (no manual predecessor)
   423→    # =============================================================================
   424→    elif use_svi and segment_idx == 0:
   425→        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_CHAINING] Seg {segment_idx}: First segment in SVI mode - using input images")
   426→        if len(orchestrator_images) > 0:
   427→            start_ref_path = orchestrator_images[0]
   428→        if len(orchestrator_images) > 1:
   429→            end_ref_path = orchestrator_images[1]
   430→
   431→    # =============================================================================
   432→    # NON-SVI MODES: Original logic
   433→    # =============================================================================
   434→    # Check individual_segment_params first (highest priority for standalone)
   435→    elif individual_params.get("start_image_url") or individual_params.get("end_image_url"):
   436→        start_ref_path = individual_params.get("start_image_url")
   437→        end_ref_path = individual_params.get("end_image_url")
   438→        task_logger.debug(f"[IMG_RESOLVE] Task {task_id}: Using individual_segment_params URLs: start={start_ref_path}")
   439→    elif len(individual_images) >= 2:
   440→        start_ref_path = individual_images[0]
   441→        end_ref_path = individual_images[1]
   442→        task_logger.debug(f"[IMG_RESOLVE] Task {task_id}: Using individual_segment_params array: start={start_ref_path}")
   443→    elif is_standalone and len(top_level_images) >= 2:
   444→        start_ref_path = top_level_images[0]
   445→        end_ref_path = top_level_images[1]
   446→        task_logger.debug(f"[IMG_RESOLVE] Task {task_id}: Using top-level images directly: start={start_ref_path}")
   447→    elif is_continuing:
   448→        if segment_idx == 0:
   449→            continued_video_path = orchestrator_details.get("continue_from_video_resolved_path")
   450→            if continued_video_path and Path(continued_video_path).exists():
   451→                start_ref_path = extract_last_frame_as_image(continued_video_path, segment_processing_dir, task_id)
   452→            if orchestrator_images:
   453→                end_ref_path = orchestrator_images[0]
   454→        else:
   455→            if len(orchestrator_images) > segment_idx:
   456→                start_ref_path = orchestrator_images[segment_idx - 1]
   457→                end_ref_path = orchestrator_images[segment_idx]
   458→    else:
   459→        task_logger.debug(f"[IMG_RESOLVE] Task {task_id}: Using orchestrator images (from scratch)")
   460→        if len(orchestrator_images) > segment_idx:
   461→            start_ref_path = orchestrator_images[segment_idx]
   462→
   463→        if len(orchestrator_images) > segment_idx + 1:
   464→            end_ref_path = orchestrator_images[segment_idx + 1]
   465→    task_logger.debug(f"[IMG_RESOLVE] Task {task_id}: start_ref_path after logic: {start_ref_path}")
   466→
   467→    if start_ref_path:
   468→        start_ref_path = download_image_if_url(start_ref_path, segment_processing_dir, task_id, debug_mode=debug_enabled)
   469→        task_logger.debug(f"[IMG_RESOLVE] Task {task_id}: start_ref_path AFTER DOWNLOAD: {start_ref_path}")
   470→    if end_ref_path:
   471→        end_ref_path = download_image_if_url(end_ref_path, segment_processing_dir, task_id, debug_mode=debug_enabled)
   472→
   473→    return ImageRefs(
   474→        start_ref_path=start_ref_path,
   475→        end_ref_path=end_ref_path,
   476→        svi_predecessor_video_for_source=svi_predecessor_video_for_source,
   477→        use_svi=use_svi,
   478→        is_continuing=is_continuing,
   479→    )
   480→
   481→
   482→def _process_structure_guidance(ctx: SegmentContext, gen: GenerationInputs, task_id: str, main_output_dir_base: Path, mask_active_frames: bool) -> StructureOutputs:
   483→    """Run TravelSegmentProcessor for VACE mode or any mode with structure guidance.
   484→
   485→    Returns StructureOutputs with guide/mask video paths and prompt type.
   486→    Raises RuntimeError/ValueError/OSError if the processor fails.
   487→    """
   488→    segment_params = ctx.segment_params
   489→    orchestrator_details = ctx.orchestrator_details
   490→    segment_idx = ctx.segment_idx
   491→    segment_processing_dir = gen.segment_processing_dir
   492→    travel_mode = gen.travel_mode
   493→    debug_enabled = gen.debug_enabled
   494→
   495→    guide_video_path = None
   496→    mask_video_path_for_wgp = None
   497→    video_prompt_type_str = None
   498→
   499→    # Always parse unified structure guidance config up-front so later logic can rely on it.
   500→    # This handles both new format (structure_guidance.videos) and legacy params (structure_videos).
   501→    structure_config = StructureGuidanceConfig.from_params({
   502→        **orchestrator_details,
   503→        **segment_params
   504→    })
   505→
   506→    # Check if structure guidance is configured (uses unified config)
   507→    has_structure_guidance = structure_config.has_guidance
   508→
   509→    # Run TravelSegmentProcessor for:
   510→    # 1. VACE mode (always - requires masks and guides)
   511→    # 2. Any mode with structure guidance configured (enables uni3c/flow guidance for i2v, etc.)
   512→    if travel_mode == "vace" or has_structure_guidance:
   513→        if has_structure_guidance and travel_mode != "vace":
   514→            task_logger.debug(f"[STRUCTURE_GUIDANCE] Task {task_id}: Running TravelSegmentProcessor for {travel_mode} mode (structure_guidance configured)")
   515→        try:
   516→            processor_context = TravelSegmentContext(
   517→                task_id=task_id,
   518→                segment_idx=segment_idx,
   519→                model_name=gen.model_name,
   520→                total_frames_for_segment=gen.total_frames_for_segment,
   521→                parsed_res_wh=gen.parsed_res_wh,
   522→                segment_processing_dir=segment_processing_dir,
   523→                main_output_dir_base=main_output_dir_base,
   524→                orchestrator_details=orchestrator_details,
   525→                segment_params=segment_params,
   526→                mask_active_frames=mask_active_frames,
   527→                debug_enabled=debug_enabled)
   528→            processor = TravelSegmentProcessor(processor_context)
   529→            segment_outputs = processor.process_segment()
   530→
   531→            guide_video_path = segment_outputs.get("video_guide")
   532→            mask_video_path_for_wgp = Path(segment_outputs["video_mask"]) if segment_outputs.get("video_mask") else None
   533→            video_prompt_type_str = segment_outputs["video_prompt_type"]
   534→            detected_structure_type = segment_outputs.get("structure_type")
   535→
   536→            # Debug: Log segment_outputs keys and structure_type
   537→            task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_DEBUG] Task {task_id}: segment_outputs keys: {list(segment_outputs.keys())}")
   538→            task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_DEBUG] Task {task_id}: detected_structure_type={repr(detected_structure_type)}, guide_video_path={bool(guide_video_path)}")
   539→
   540→            # If config targets uni3c and we have a guide video, update the config's guidance URL
   541→            # This is used later by the UNI3C MODE section
   542→            if structure_config.is_uni3c and guide_video_path:
   543→                task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_AUTO] Task {task_id}: Uni3C mode with guide from processor: {guide_video_path}")
   544→                # Store the processor's guide video path in the config
   545→                structure_config._guidance_video_url = guide_video_path
   546→
   547→        except (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError) as e_shared_processor:
   548→            task_logger.error(f"Shared processor failed: {e_shared_processor}", exc_info=True)
   549→            raise RuntimeError(f"Shared processor failed: {e_shared_processor}") from e_shared_processor
   550→
   551→    return StructureOutputs(
   552→        guide_video_path=guide_video_path,
   553→        mask_video_path_for_wgp=mask_video_path_for_wgp,
   554→        video_prompt_type_str=video_prompt_type_str,
   555→        structure_config=structure_config,
   556→    )
   557→
   558→
   559→def _build_generation_params(ctx: SegmentContext, gen: GenerationInputs, image_refs: ImageRefs, structure: StructureOutputs, task_id: str) -> dict:
   560→    """Build the WGP generation_params dict from resolved inputs.
   561→
   562→    Handles base params, image paths, additional_loras, explicit overrides
   563→    (num_inference_steps, guidance_scale, flow_shift), per-segment LoRAs,
   564→    phase_config parsing, and guide/mask video attachment.
   565→    """
   566→    segment_params = ctx.segment_params
   567→    orchestrator_details = ctx.orchestrator_details
   568→    individual_params = ctx.individual_params
   569→    debug_enabled = gen.debug_enabled
   570→    model_name = gen.model_name
   571→    start_ref_path = image_refs.start_ref_path
   572→    end_ref_path = image_refs.end_ref_path
   573→    guide_video_path = structure.guide_video_path
   574→    mask_video_path_for_wgp = structure.mask_video_path_for_wgp
   575→    video_prompt_type_str = structure.video_prompt_type_str
   576→    structure_config = structure.structure_config
   577→
   578→    # Seed: individual_segment_params > top-level > default
   579→    seed_to_use = individual_params.get("seed_to_use") or segment_params.get("seed_to_use", 12345)
   580→
   581→    generation_params = {
   582→        "model_name": model_name,
   583→        "negative_prompt": gen.negative_prompt_for_wgp,
   584→        "resolution": f"{gen.parsed_res_wh[0]}x{gen.parsed_res_wh[1]}",
   585→        "video_length": gen.total_frames_for_segment,
   586→        "seed": seed_to_use,
   587→    }
   588→
   589→    # Always pass images if available, regardless of specific travel_mode string (hybrid models need them)
   590→    if start_ref_path:
   591→        generation_params["image_start"] = str(Path(start_ref_path).resolve())
   592→    if end_ref_path:
   593→        generation_params["image_end"] = str(Path(end_ref_path).resolve())
   594→
   595→    task_logger.debug(f"[IMG_RESOLVE] Task {task_id}: generation_params image_start: {generation_params.get('image_start')}")
   596→    task_logger.debug(f"[IMG_RESOLVE] Task {task_id}: generation_params image_end: {generation_params.get('image_end')}")
   597→
   598→    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   599→    # Parameter extraction with precedence: individual > segment > orchestrator
   600→    # Using _get_param() helper for consistent fallback behavior
   601→    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   602→
   603→    # Travel-only: pass `additional_loras` through on the segment task payload if present,
   604→    # but DO NOT propagate into `generation_params` (so it won't trigger LoRA downloads/application).
   605→    additional_loras = _get_param(
   606→        "additional_loras",
   607→        individual_params,
   608→        segment_params,
   609→        orchestrator_details,
   610→        default={},
   611→        prefer_truthy=True,  # match previous `a or b or c` behavior for empty dicts
   612→    )
   613→    if additional_loras and debug_enabled:
   614→        task_logger.debug(
   615→            f"[TRAVEL_LORA] Task {task_id}: additional_loras present on payload but intentionally ignored for generation ({len(additional_loras)} entries)"
   616→        )
   617→
   618→    # IMPORTANT: Do NOT treat orchestrator/UI `steps` as diffusion `num_inference_steps`.
   619→    # In travel payloads, `steps` often means "timeline steps" (UI concept), whereas
   620→    # diffusion steps must come from `num_inference_steps` (or `phase_config.steps_per_phase`).
   621→    explicit_steps = _get_param("num_inference_steps", segment_params, orchestrator_details, prefer_truthy=True)
   622→    if explicit_steps:
   623→        generation_params["num_inference_steps"] = explicit_steps
   624→
   625→    explicit_guidance = _get_param("guidance_scale", segment_params, orchestrator_details, prefer_truthy=True)
   626→    if explicit_guidance:
   627→        generation_params["guidance_scale"] = explicit_guidance
   628→
   629→    explicit_flow_shift = _get_param("flow_shift", segment_params, orchestrator_details, prefer_truthy=True)
   630→    if explicit_flow_shift:
   631→        generation_params["flow_shift"] = explicit_flow_shift
   632→
   633→    # =============================================================================
   634→    # Per-Segment Parameter Overrides
   635→    # =============================================================================
   636→    # Log what per-segment overrides were received
   637→    task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_HANDLER] Task {task_id}: ========== Per-Segment Override Check ==========")
   638→    task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_HANDLER] Task {task_id}: individual_params keys: {list(individual_params.keys()) if individual_params else 'None'}")
   639→
   640→    # Check for segment-specific LoRAs first (highest priority)
   641→    # This allows per-segment LoRA overrides to take precedence over phase_config LoRAs
   642→    segment_loras = _get_param("segment_loras", individual_params, default=None)
   643→    segment_lora_config = None
   644→
   645→    if segment_loras:
   646→        task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_LORAS] Task {task_id}: Using segment-specific LoRAs ({len(segment_loras)} LoRAs)")
   647→        # Pass through URLs/filenames without downloading - convert_to_wgp_task_impl() handles resolution
   648→        segment_lora_config = True  # Flag to skip phase_config LoRAs below
   649→        activated = []
   650→        mults = []
   651→        for lora_dict in segment_loras:
   652→            path = lora_dict.get("path", "")
   653→            strength = lora_dict.get("strength", 1.0)
   654→            if path:
   655→                activated.append(path)
   656→                mults.append(str(strength))
   657→        if activated:
   658→            generation_params["activated_loras"] = activated
   659→            generation_params["loras_multipliers"] = " ".join(mults)
   660→            headless_logger.info(f"Set {len(activated)} segment-specific LoRAs (download deferred)", task_id=task_id)
   661→    else:
   662→        task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_LORAS] Task {task_id}: No segment-specific LoRAs - will use phase_config/shot-level LoRAs if present")
   663→
   664→    # Determine phase_config source for logging
   665→    phase_config_from_individual = individual_params.get("phase_config") if individual_params else None
   666→    phase_config_from_segment = segment_params.get("phase_config") if segment_params else None
   667→    _phase_config_from_orchestrator = orchestrator_details.get("phase_config") if orchestrator_details else None
   668→
   669→    phase_config_source = _get_param(
   670→        "phase_config", individual_params, segment_params, orchestrator_details, prefer_truthy=True
   671→    )
   672→
   673→    # Log which source phase_config came from
   674→    if phase_config_source:
   675→        if phase_config_from_individual:
   676→            source_name = "PER-SEGMENT (individual_params)"
   677→        elif phase_config_from_segment:
   678→            source_name = "segment_params"
   679→        else:
   680→            source_name = "SHOT-LEVEL (orchestrator_details)"
   681→
   682→        preset_name = phase_config_source.get("preset_name", phase_config_source.get("name", "unknown"))
   683→        task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_PHASE_CONFIG] Task {task_id}: Using phase_config from {source_name}")
   684→        task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_PHASE_CONFIG] Task {task_id}: preset_name={preset_name}")
   685→
   686→    if phase_config_source:
   687→        try:
   688→            steps_per_phase = phase_config_source.get("steps_per_phase", [2, 2, 2])
   689→            phase_config_steps = sum(steps_per_phase)
   690→            task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_PHASE_CONFIG] Task {task_id}: steps_per_phase={steps_per_phase} (total={phase_config_steps})")
   691→
   692→            parsed_phase_config = parse_phase_config(
   693→                phase_config=phase_config_source,
   694→                num_inference_steps=phase_config_steps,
   695→                task_id=task_id,
   696→                model_name=generation_params.get("model_name"),
   697→                debug_mode=debug_enabled
   698→            )
   699→
   700→            generation_params["num_inference_steps"] = phase_config_steps
   701→
   702→            # Copy non-LoRA params from phase_config
   703→            for key in ["guidance_phases", "switch_threshold", "switch_threshold2",
   704→                       "guidance_scale", "guidance2_scale", "guidance3_scale",
   705→                       "flow_shift", "sample_solver", "model_switch_phase"]:
   706→                if key in parsed_phase_config and parsed_phase_config[key] is not None:
   707→                    generation_params[key] = parsed_phase_config[key]
   708→
   709→            # Copy LoRA params from phase_config ONLY if no segment-specific LoRAs
   710→            # (segment_loras takes precedence over phase_config LoRAs)
   711→            # Pass through URLs without downloading - convert_to_wgp_task_impl() handles resolution
   712→            if not segment_lora_config:
   713→                if "lora_names" in parsed_phase_config:
   714→                    generation_params["activated_loras"] = parsed_phase_config["lora_names"]
   715→                if "lora_multipliers" in parsed_phase_config:
   716→                    generation_params["loras_multipliers"] = " ".join(str(m) for m in parsed_phase_config["lora_multipliers"])
   717→                lora_count = len(parsed_phase_config.get("lora_names", []))
   718→                if lora_count:
   719→                    headless_logger.info(f"Set {lora_count} phase_config LoRAs (download deferred)", task_id=task_id)
   720→            else:
   721→                task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_PHASE_CONFIG] Task {task_id}: Skipping phase_config LoRAs (segment-specific LoRAs take precedence)")
   722→
   723→            # Pass phase_config patch data through to task_processor.py for proper apply+restore lifecycle
   724→            # (instead of applying directly here where it would never be cleaned up)
   725→            if "_patch_config" in parsed_phase_config:
   726→                generation_params["_parsed_phase_config"] = parsed_phase_config
   727→                generation_params["_phase_config_model_name"] = model_name
   728→
   729→        except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
   730→            raise ValueError(f"Task {task_id}: Invalid phase_config: {e}") from e
   731→    else:
   732→        task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_PHASE_CONFIG] Task {task_id}: No phase_config found - using explicit params only")
   733→
   734→    # Summary log for per-segment overrides
   735→    task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_HANDLER] Task {task_id}: ========== Per-Segment Override Summary ==========")
   736→    task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_HANDLER] Task {task_id}: LoRAs applied: {generation_params.get('activated_loras', [])}")
   737→    task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_HANDLER] Task {task_id}: LoRA multipliers: {generation_params.get('loras_multipliers', '')}")
   738→    task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_HANDLER] Task {task_id}: num_inference_steps: {generation_params.get('num_inference_steps', 'not set')}")
   739→    task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_HANDLER] Task {task_id}: guidance_scale: {generation_params.get('guidance_scale', 'not set')}")
   740→    task_logger.debug(f"[PER_SEGMENT_HANDLER] Task {task_id}: ================================================")
   741→
   742→    if guide_video_path: generation_params["video_guide"] = str(guide_video_path)
   743→    if mask_video_path_for_wgp: generation_params["video_mask"] = str(mask_video_path_for_wgp.resolve())
   744→    generation_params["video_prompt_type"] = video_prompt_type_str
   745→
   746→    # Diagnostic: Log guidance configuration when uni3c is enabled
   747→    if structure_config.is_uni3c and guide_video_path:
   748→        task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_GUIDANCE_CHECK] Task {task_id}: Checking guidance configuration...")
   749→        task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_GUIDANCE_CHECK]   video_guide path: {guide_video_path}")
   750→        task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_GUIDANCE_CHECK]   structure_config.guidance_video_url: {structure_config.guidance_video_url}")
   751→        task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_GUIDANCE_CHECK]   image_end (i2v): {generation_params.get('image_end', 'None')}")
   752→        task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_GUIDANCE_CHECK]   video_prompt_type: '{video_prompt_type_str}'")
   753→        if "V" in video_prompt_type_str:
   754→            task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_GUIDANCE_CHECK]   🔴 WARNING: video_prompt_type has 'V' - VACE will ALSO use video_guide!")
   755→            task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_GUIDANCE_CHECK]   This causes double-feeding: both VACE and Uni3C use same guide")
   756→        else:
   757→            task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_GUIDANCE_CHECK]   ✅ OK: video_prompt_type='{video_prompt_type_str}' (no 'V')")
   758→            task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_GUIDANCE_CHECK]   Uni3C handles motion guidance, VACE only uses mask for frame preservation")
   759→
   760→    return generation_params
   761→
   762→
   763→def _apply_svi_config(generation_params: dict, ctx: SegmentContext, gen: GenerationInputs, image_refs: ImageRefs, task_id: str) -> None:
   764→    """Apply SVI-specific generation parameters (mutates generation_params in place).
   765→
   766→    Enables SVI encoding mode, sets video_prompt_type, configures predecessor video
   767→    as video_source, adjusts video_length for continuation frame accounting,
   768→    copies SVI generation params, and merges SVI LoRAs.
   769→    """
   770→    if not image_refs.use_svi:
   771→        return
   772→
   773→    segment_params = ctx.segment_params
   774→    orchestrator_details = ctx.orchestrator_details
   775→    start_ref_path = image_refs.start_ref_path
   776→    svi_predecessor_video_for_source = image_refs.svi_predecessor_video_for_source
   777→    total_frames_for_segment = gen.total_frames_for_segment
   778→
   779→    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: Configuring WGP payload for SVI mode")
   780→
   781→    # Enable SVI encoding mode
   782→    generation_params["svi2pro"] = True
   783→
   784→    # SVI requires video_prompt_type="I" to enable image_refs passthrough
   785→    generation_params["video_prompt_type"] = "I"
   786→
   787→    # Set image_refs to start image (anchor for SVI encoding)
   788→    if start_ref_path:
   789→        generation_params["image_refs_paths"] = [str(Path(start_ref_path).resolve())]
   790→        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: Set image_refs_paths to start image: {start_ref_path}")
   791→
   792→    # CRITICAL: Pass predecessor video as video_source for SVI continuation
   793→    # WGP uses prefix_video[:, -(5 + overlap_size):] to create overlapped_latents
   794→    # This provides temporal continuity between segments (uses last ~9 frames)
   795→    # IMPORTANT: Must NOT set image_start when video_source is set, otherwise
   796→    # wgp.py prioritizes image_start and creates only a 1-frame prefix_video!
   797→    if svi_predecessor_video_for_source:
   798→        from source.media.video import get_video_frame_count_and_fps as get_video_frame_count_and_fps
   799→
   800→        video_source_path = str(Path(svi_predecessor_video_for_source).resolve())
   801→        generation_params["video_source"] = video_source_path
   802→
   803→        # GROUND TRUTH LOG: What WGP will receive
   804→        try:
   805→            wgp_input_frames, wgp_input_fps = get_video_frame_count_and_fps(video_source_path)
   806→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Task {task_id}: ========== WGP INPUT ANALYSIS ==========")
   807→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Task {task_id}: video_source: {video_source_path}")
   808→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Task {task_id}: video_source frames: {wgp_input_frames}")
   809→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Task {task_id}: WGP will extract last 9 frames from this for overlapped_latents")
   810→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Task {task_id}: WGP will prepend ALL {wgp_input_frames} frames to output")
   811→        except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as e_wgp_log:
   812→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_GROUND_TRUTH] Task {task_id}: Could not analyze video_source: {e_wgp_log}")
   813→
   814→        # Remove image_start so WGP uses video_source for multi-frame prefix_video
   815→        # The anchor image is provided via image_refs instead
   816→        if "image_start" in generation_params:
   817→            del generation_params["image_start"]
   818→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: Removed image_start (anchor provided via image_refs)")
   819→        # CRITICAL: Set image_prompt_type to include "V" to enable video_source usage
   820→        # SVI2Pro allows "SVL" - we use "SV" for start+video continuation
   821→        generation_params["image_prompt_type"] = "SV"
   822→        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: Set image_prompt_type='SV' for video continuation")
   823→        task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: Set video_source for SVI continuation: {svi_predecessor_video_for_source}")
   824→
   825→    # SVI Pro sliding window overlap = 4 frames (standard for SVI)
   826→    # Note: WGP applies latent alignment formula (x-1)//4*4+1, but we bypass it
   827→    # by patching sliding_window_defaults.overlap_default=4 in headless_model_management.py
   828→    generation_params["sliding_window_overlap"] = 4
   829→    task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: Set sliding_window_overlap=4 for SVI")
   830→
   831→    # IMPORTANT (SVI continuation frame accounting):
   832→    # When `video_source` is provided, WGP will:
   833→    #   - generate `video_length` frames total
   834→    #   - discard the first `sliding_window_overlap` frames of the generated sample
   835→    #   - prepend the prefix video frames (pixels) to the output
   836→    #
   837→    # Therefore the number of **new** frames produced by diffusion is:
   838→    #   new_frames = video_length - sliding_window_overlap
   839→    #
   840→    # In our travel pipeline, `segment_frames_target` / `segment_frames_expanded[idx]` represent
   841→    # the desired number of **new** frames for the segment (4N+1). To actually get that many
   842→    # new frames while still maintaining overlap for stitching, we must request:
   843→    #   video_length = desired_new_frames + sliding_window_overlap
   844→    if svi_predecessor_video_for_source:
   845→        try:
   846→            desired_new_frames = int(total_frames_for_segment) if total_frames_for_segment else 0
   847→            overlap_size = int(generation_params.get("sliding_window_overlap") or 4)
   848→            current_video_length = int(generation_params.get("video_length") or 0)
   849→            if desired_new_frames > 0 and overlap_size > 0:
   850→                # Only bump if the payload is still "new-frames based" (avoid double-bumping).
   851→                if current_video_length == desired_new_frames:
   852→                    generation_params["video_length"] = desired_new_frames + overlap_size
   853→                    task_logger.debug(
   854→                        f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: SVI continuation => bump video_length "
   855→                        f"{current_video_length} -> {generation_params['video_length']} "
   856→                        f"(desired_new_frames={desired_new_frames}, overlap_size={overlap_size})"
   857→                    )
   858→                else:
   859→                    task_logger.debug(
   860→                        f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: SVI continuation => NOT bumping video_length "
   861→                        f"(current={current_video_length}, desired_new_frames={desired_new_frames}, overlap_size={overlap_size})"
   862→                    )
   863→        except (ValueError, TypeError) as e_len_bump:
   864→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: WARNING: Could not adjust video_length for SVI continuation: {e_len_bump}")
   865→
   866→    # Add SVI generation parameters from segment_params (set by orchestrator)
   867→    for key in ["guidance_phases", "num_inference_steps", "guidance_scale", "guidance2_scale",
   868→               "flow_shift", "switch_threshold", "model_switch_phase", "sample_solver"]:
   869→        if key in segment_params and segment_params[key] is not None:
   870→            generation_params[key] = segment_params[key]
   871→            task_logger.debug(f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: Set {key}={segment_params[key]}")
   872→
   873→    # Merge SVI LoRAs with existing LoRAs
   874→    from source.task_handlers.travel.svi_config import merge_svi_into_generation_params
   875→
   876→    svi_strength = _get_param("svi_strength", segment_params, orchestrator_details)
   877→    svi_strength_1 = _get_param("svi_strength_1", segment_params, orchestrator_details)
   878→    svi_strength_2 = _get_param("svi_strength_2", segment_params, orchestrator_details)
   879→
   880→    merge_svi_into_generation_params(
   881→        generation_params,
   882→        svi_strength=svi_strength,
   883→        svi_strength_1=svi_strength_1,
   884→        svi_strength_2=svi_strength_2)
   885→
   886→    task_logger.debug(
   887→        f"[SVI_PAYLOAD] Task {task_id}: Merged SVI LoRAs "
   888→        f"(svi_strength={svi_strength}, svi_strength_1={svi_strength_1}, svi_strength_2={svi_strength_2})"
   889→    )
   890→
   891→
   892→def _apply_uni3c_config(generation_params: dict, ctx: SegmentContext, gen: GenerationInputs, structure: StructureOutputs, task_id: str) -> None:
   893→    """Apply UNI3C-specific generation parameters (mutates generation_params in place).
   894→
   895→    Downloads the guide video if it is a URL, then injects all uni3c_* parameters
   896→    into generation_params.
   897→    """
   898→    structure_config = structure.structure_config
   899→    segment_params = ctx.segment_params
   900→    segment_processing_dir = gen.segment_processing_dir
   901→
   902→    # Use unified structure_config exclusively
   903→    use_uni3c = structure_config.is_uni3c
   904→
   905→    task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C_DEBUG] Task {task_id}: structure_config.is_uni3c={structure_config.is_uni3c}, use_uni3c={use_uni3c}")
   906→
   907→    if not use_uni3c:
   908→        return
   909→
   910→    from source.utils import download_file as download_file
   911→
   912→    # Get guide video from config (may have been set by processor)
   913→    uni3c_guide = structure_config.guidance_video_url
   914→
   915→    # If Uni3C is enabled but there's no guide video, skip to avoid downstream crashes.
   916→    if not uni3c_guide:
   917→        task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}: Uni3C requested but no guide video provided; skipping Uni3C injection")
   918→        return
   919→
   920→    # Use config values (already handles legacy param fallback)
   921→    uni3c_strength = structure_config.strength
   922→    uni3c_start = structure_config.step_window[0]
   923→    uni3c_end = structure_config.step_window[1]
   924→    uni3c_keep_gpu = structure_config.keep_on_gpu
   925→    uni3c_frame_policy = structure_config.frame_policy
   926→    uni3c_zero_empty = structure_config.zero_empty_frames
   927→
   928→    # Download guide video if URL
   929→    if uni3c_guide.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
   930→        local_filename = Path(uni3c_guide).name or "uni3c_guide_video.mp4"
   931→        local_download_path = segment_processing_dir / f"uni3c_{local_filename}"
   932→        if not local_download_path.exists():
   933→            download_file(uni3c_guide, segment_processing_dir, local_download_path.name)
   934→            task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}: Downloaded guide video to {local_download_path}")
   935→        else:
   936→            task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}: Guide video already exists at {local_download_path}")
   937→        uni3c_guide = str(local_download_path)
   938→
   939→    # Layer 2 logging
   940→    task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}: Uni3C ENABLED (via structure_guidance config)")
   941→    task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}:   guide_video={uni3c_guide}")
   942→    task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}:   strength={uni3c_strength}")
   943→    task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}:   start_percent={uni3c_start}")
   944→    task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}:   end_percent={uni3c_end}")
   945→    task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}:   frame_policy={uni3c_frame_policy}")
   946→    task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}:   keep_on_gpu={uni3c_keep_gpu}")
   947→    task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}:   zero_empty_frames={uni3c_zero_empty}")
   948→
   949→    # Inject into generation_params
   950→    generation_params["use_uni3c"] = True
   951→    generation_params["uni3c_guide_video"] = uni3c_guide
   952→    generation_params["uni3c_strength"] = uni3c_strength
   953→    generation_params["uni3c_start_percent"] = uni3c_start
   954→    generation_params["uni3c_end_percent"] = uni3c_end
   955→    generation_params["uni3c_keep_on_gpu"] = uni3c_keep_gpu
   956→    generation_params["uni3c_frame_policy"] = uni3c_frame_policy
   957→    generation_params["uni3c_zero_empty_frames"] = uni3c_zero_empty
   958→
   959→    # For i2v with end anchor: blackout last uni3c frame so i2v handles it alone
   960→    # This prevents uni3c from "overcooking" the final frame
   961→    is_last_segment = segment_params.get("is_last_segment", True)
   962→    has_end_anchor = generation_params.get("image_end") is not None
   963→    if is_last_segment and has_end_anchor:
   964→        generation_params["uni3c_blackout_last_frame"] = True
   965→        task_logger.debug(f"[UNI3C] Task {task_id}: Will blackout last frame (is_last_segment + has end anchor)")
   966→
   967→
   968→def handle_travel_segment_via_queue(task_params_dict: dict, main_output_dir_base: Path, task_id: str, colour_match_videos: bool, mask_active_frames: bool, task_queue: HeadlessTaskQueue, is_standalone: bool = False):
   969→    """Handle travel segment tasks via direct queue integration to eliminate blocking waits.
   970→
   971→    Orchestrator mode (is_standalone=False) requires orchestrator_task_id_ref, orchestrator_run_id, segment_index.
   972→    Standalone mode (is_standalone=True) uses orchestrator_details provided directly in params.
   973→    Parameter precedence: individual_segment_params > segment_params > orchestrator_details.
   974→    """
   975→    headless_logger.debug(f"Starting travel segment queue processing (standalone={is_standalone})", task_id=task_id)
   976→    log_ram_usage("Segment via queue - start", task_id=task_id)
   977→
   978→    try:
   979→        from source.task_handlers.travel.chaining import _handle_travel_chaining_after_wgp
   980→
   981→        # 1. Resolve segment context (mode, orchestrator_details, individual_params, segment_idx)
   982→        ctx = _resolve_segment_context(task_params_dict, is_standalone, task_id)
   983→
   984→        # 2. Resolve generation inputs (model, prompt, resolution, frames, output dir, flags)
   985→        gen = _resolve_generation_inputs(ctx, task_id, main_output_dir_base)
   986→
   987→        # 3. Resolve image references (SVI chaining, non-SVI image resolution, downloading)
   988→        image_refs = _resolve_image_references(ctx, gen, task_id, is_standalone)
   989→
   990→        # 4. Process structure guidance (TravelSegmentProcessor)
   991→        structure = _process_structure_guidance(ctx, gen, task_id, main_output_dir_base, mask_active_frames)
   992→
   993→        # 5. Build generation_params dict
   994→        generation_params = _build_generation_params(ctx, gen, image_refs, structure, task_id)
   995→
   996→        # 6. Apply SVI-specific configuration
   997→        _apply_svi_config(generation_params, ctx, gen, image_refs, task_id)
   998→        # 7. Apply UNI3C-specific configuration
   999→        _apply_uni3c_config(generation_params, ctx, gen, structure, task_id)
  1000→
  1001→        # Log diagnostic summary before WGP submission
  1002→        task_logger.debug(f"[WGP_SUBMIT] Task {task_id}: ========== WGP GENERATION REQUEST ==========")
  1003→        task_logger.debug(f"[WGP_SUBMIT] Task {task_id}: video_length (target frames): {generation_params.get('video_length')}")
  1004→        is_valid_4n1 = (generation_params.get('video_length', 0) - 1) % 4 == 0
  1005→        task_logger.debug(f"[WGP_SUBMIT] Task {task_id}: Valid 4N+1: {is_valid_4n1} {'✓' if is_valid_4n1 else '✗ WARNING'}")
  1006→        task_logger.debug(f"[WGP_SUBMIT] Task {task_id}: video_guide: {generation_params.get('video_guide', 'None')}")
  1007→        task_logger.debug(f"[WGP_SUBMIT] Task {task_id}: video_mask: {generation_params.get('video_mask', 'None')}")
  1008→        task_logger.debug(f"[WGP_SUBMIT] Task {task_id}: model: {gen.model_name}")
  1009→        task_logger.debug(f"[WGP_SUBMIT] Task {task_id}: resolution: {generation_params.get('resolution')}")
  1010→        task_logger.debug(f"[WGP_SUBMIT] Task {task_id}: =============================================")
  1011→
  1012→        # IMPORTANT: Use the DB task_id as the queue task id.
  1013→        # This keeps logs, fatal error handling, and debug tooling consistent (no "travel_seg_" indirection).
  1014→        # We still include a hint in parameters so the queue can apply any task-type specific behavior.
  1015→        generation_params["_source_task_type"] = "travel_segment"
  1016→        generation_task = GenerationTask(
  1017→            id=task_id,
  1018→            model=gen.model_name,
  1019→            prompt=gen.prompt_for_wgp,
  1020→            parameters=generation_params
  1021→        )
  1022→
  1023→        _submitted_task_id = task_queue.submit_task(generation_task)
  1024→
  1025→        max_wait_time = 1800
  1026→        wait_interval = 2
  1027→        elapsed_time = 0
  1028→
  1029→        while elapsed_time < max_wait_time:
  1030→            status = task_queue.get_task_status(task_id)
  1031→            if status is None: return False, f"Travel segment {task_id}: Task status became None"
  1032→
  1033→            if status.status == "completed":
  1034→                # In standalone mode, skip chaining (no orchestrator to coordinate with)
  1035→                if is_standalone:
  1036→                    headless_logger.debug(f"Standalone segment completed, skipping chaining", task_id=task_id)
  1037→                    return True, status.result_path
  1038→
  1039→                # Orchestrator mode: run chaining
  1040→                chain_success, chain_message, final_chained_path = _handle_travel_chaining_after_wgp(
  1041→                    wgp_task_params={
  1042→                        # Provide minimal ground-truth frame params for downstream debug logging / trimming analysis.
  1043→                        "use_svi": image_refs.use_svi,
  1044→                        "video_length": generation_params.get("video_length"),
  1045→                        "sliding_window_overlap": generation_params.get("sliding_window_overlap"),
  1046→                        "video_source": generation_params.get("video_source"),
  1047→                        "travel_chain_details": {
  1048→                            "orchestrator_task_id_ref": ctx.orchestrator_task_id_ref,
  1049→                            "orchestrator_run_id": ctx.orchestrator_run_id,
  1050→                            "segment_index_completed": ctx.segment_idx,
  1051→                            "orchestrator_details": ctx.orchestrator_details,
  1052→                            "segment_processing_dir_for_saturation": str(gen.segment_processing_dir),
  1053→                            "is_first_new_segment_after_continue": ctx.segment_params.get("is_first_segment", False) and ctx.orchestrator_details.get("continue_from_video_resolved_path"),
  1054→                            "is_subsequent_segment": not ctx.segment_params.get("is_first_segment", True),
  1055→                            "colour_match_videos": colour_match_videos,
  1056→                            "cm_start_ref_path": None, "cm_end_ref_path": None, "show_input_images": False, "start_image_path": None, "end_image_path": None,
  1057→                        }
  1058→                    },
  1059→                    actual_wgp_output_video_path=status.result_path,
  1060→                    image_download_dir=gen.segment_processing_dir,
  1061→                    main_output_dir_base=main_output_dir_base)

  1215→            
  1216→            task_queue.submit_task(generation_task)
  1217→

  1219→            max_wait_time = 3600
  1220→            elapsed = 0

  1222→                status = task_queue.get_task_status(task_id)

  1233→            return False, "Timeout"
```

```
   443→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   444→# Worker loop
   445→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   446→
   447→def worker_loop(queue: "HeadlessTaskQueue"):
   448→    """Main worker loop for processing tasks."""
   449→    import threading
   450→    worker_name = threading.current_thread().name
   451→    queue.logger.info(f"{worker_name} started")
   452→
   453→    while queue.running and not queue.shutdown_event.is_set():
   454→        try:
   455→            # Get next task (blocks with timeout)
   456→            try:
   457→                priority, timestamp, task = queue.task_queue.get(timeout=1.0)
   458→            except queue_mod.Empty:
   459→                continue
   460→
   461→            # Process the task
   462→            process_task_impl(queue, task, worker_name)
   463→
   464→        except (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError) as e:
   465→            queue.logger.error(f"{worker_name} error: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}")
   466→            time.sleep(1.0)
   467→
   468→    queue.logger.info(f"{worker_name} stopped")
   469→
   470→
   471→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   472→# Monitor loop
   473→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   474→
   475→def _monitor_loop(queue: "HeadlessTaskQueue"):
   476→    """Background monitoring and maintenance loop."""
   477→    queue.logger.info("Queue monitor started")
   478→
   479→    while queue.running and not queue.shutdown_event.is_set():
   480→        try:
   481→            # Monitor loop placeholder - future home for memory/queue/timeout monitoring
   482→            time.sleep(10.0)  # Monitor every 10 seconds
   483→
   484→        except (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError) as e:
   485→            queue.logger.error(f"Monitor error: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}")
   486→            time.sleep(5.0)
   487→
   488→    queue.logger.info("Queue monitor stopped")
```

```
    95→            return output_path
    96→

   100→            headless_logger.debug(f"Output already in subdirectory, skipping move: {output_path}", task_id=task_id)

   112→        # Move the file

   333→    finally:

   336→    # Clean up legacy collision-prone LoRA files
   337→    cleanup_legacy_lora_collisions()

   339→    # Initialize Task Queue

   348→        task_queue.start(preload_model=preload_model)
   349→    except (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError) as e:

   351→        sys.exit(1)
   352→
   353→    headless_logger.essential(f"Worker {cli_args.worker or 'anonymous'} started. Polling every {cli_args.poll_interval}s.")
   354→
   355→    try:
   356→        while True:
   357→            task_info = db_ops.get_oldest_queued_task_supabase(worker_id=cli_args.worker)
   358→
   359→            if not task_info:
   360→                time.sleep(cli_args.poll_interval)
   361→                continue
   362→
   363→            current_task_params = task_info["params"]
   364→            current_task_type = task_info["task_type"]
   365→            current_project_id = task_info.get("project_id")
   366→            current_task_id = task_info["task_id"]
   367→
   368→            if current_project_id is None and current_task_type in {"travel_orchestrator", "edit_video_orchestrator"}:
   369→                db_ops.update_task_status_supabase(current_task_id, db_ops.STATUS_FAILED, "Orchestrator missing project_id")
   370→                continue
   371→
   372→            # Ensure params["task_id"] is the DB UUID (not the human-readable params.task_id)
   373→            # process_single_task reads task_id from params, so this must be set for ALL task types
   374→            current_task_params["task_id"] = current_task_id
   375→            if "orchestrator_details" in current_task_params:
   376→                current_task_params["orchestrator_details"]["orchestrator_task_id"] = current_task_id
   377→

   379→            if _log_interceptor_instance:

   381→
   382→            task_succeeded, output_location = process_single_task(

   384→                image_download_dir=current_task_params.get("segment_image_download_dir"),
   385→                colour_match_videos=cli_args.colour_match_videos,

   387→                task_queue=task_queue
   388→            )

   390→            if task_succeeded:

   392→
   393→                orchestrator_types = {"travel_orchestrator", "join_clips_orchestrator", "edit_video_orchestrator"}
   394→
   395→                if current_task_type in orchestrator_types:
   396→                    if output_location and output_location.startswith("[ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE]"):
   397→                        actual_output = output_location.replace("[ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE]", "")
   398→                        thumbnail_url = None
   399→                        try:

   401→                            data = json.loads(actual_output)
   402→                            actual_output = data.get("output_location", actual_output)
   403→                            thumbnail_url = data.get("thumbnail_url")
   404→                        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, KeyError):
   405→                            pass  # actual_output is a plain string, not JSON - use as-is
   406→                        
   407→                        db_ops.update_task_status_supabase(current_task_id, db_ops.STATUS_COMPLETE, actual_output, thumbnail_url)
   408→                    else:
   409→                        db_ops.update_task_status(current_task_id, db_ops.STATUS_IN_PROGRESS, output_location)
   410→                else:
   411→                    db_ops.update_task_status_supabase(current_task_id, db_ops.STATUS_COMPLETE, output_location)
   412→                    
   413→                    # Note: Orchestrator completion is handled by the complete-task Edge Function

   415→                    
   416→                    cleanup_generated_files(output_location, current_task_id, debug_mode)
   417→            else:
   418→                # Task failed - check if this is a retryable error
   419→                error_message = output_location or "Unknown error"

   421→                current_attempts = task_info.get("attempts", 0)
   422→                
   423→                if is_retryable and current_attempts < max_attempts:
   424→                    # Requeue for retry
   425→                    headless_logger.warning(

   427→                        f"requeuing for retry (attempt {current_attempts + 1}/{max_attempts})"
   428→                    )
   429→                    db_ops.requeue_task_for_retry(
   430→                        current_task_id, 
   431→                        error_message, 
   432→                        current_attempts, 
   433→                        error_category
   434→                    )
   435→                else:
   436→                    # Permanent failure - either not retryable or exhausted retries
   437→                    if is_retryable and current_attempts >= max_attempts:
   438→                        headless_logger.error(
   439→                            f"Task {current_task_id} exhausted {max_attempts} retry attempts for {error_category}"
   440→                        )
   441→                    db_ops.update_task_status_supabase(current_task_id, db_ops.STATUS_FAILED, output_location)
   442→            
   443→            # Clear task context from log interceptor
   444→            if _log_interceptor_instance:
```

```
    21→def _check_orchestrator_cancelled(orchestrator_task_id: str, context_msg: str, **_kwargs) -> str | None:
    22→    """Check if orchestrator was cancelled and cancel children if so.
    23→
    24→    Returns an error message string if cancelled, None if still active.
    25→    """
    26→    status = db_ops.get_task_current_status(orchestrator_task_id)
    27→    if status and status.lower() in ('cancelled', 'canceled'):
    28→        task_logger.debug(f"[CANCELLATION] Join orchestrator {orchestrator_task_id} was cancelled - {context_msg}", task_id=orchestrator_task_id)
    29→        db_ops.cancel_orchestrator_children(orchestrator_task_id, reason="Orchestrator cancelled by user")
    30→        return f"Orchestrator cancelled: {context_msg}"
    31→    return None
    32→
    33→
    34→def _extract_join_settings_from_payload(orchestrator_payload: dict) -> dict:
    35→    """
    36→    Extract standardized join settings from an orchestrator payload.
    37→
    38→    Used by both join_clips_orchestrator and edit_video_orchestrator.
    39→
    40→    Args:
    41→        orchestrator_payload: The orchestrator_details dict
    42→
    43→    Returns:
    44→        Dict of join settings for join_clips_segment tasks
    45→    """
    46→    use_input_res = orchestrator_payload.get("use_input_video_resolution", False)
    47→
    48→    return {
    49→        "context_frame_count": orchestrator_payload.get("context_frame_count", 8),
    50→        "gap_frame_count": orchestrator_payload.get("gap_frame_count", 53),
    51→        "replace_mode": orchestrator_payload.get("replace_mode", False),
    52→        "prompt": orchestrator_payload.get("prompt", "smooth transition"),
    53→        "negative_prompt": orchestrator_payload.get("negative_prompt", ""),
    54→        "model": orchestrator_payload.get("model", "wan_2_2_vace_lightning_baseline_2_2_2"),
    55→        "aspect_ratio": orchestrator_payload.get("aspect_ratio"),
    56→        "resolution": None if use_input_res else orchestrator_payload.get("resolution"),
    57→        "use_input_video_resolution": use_input_res,
    58→        "fps": orchestrator_payload.get("fps"),
    59→        "use_input_video_fps": orchestrator_payload.get("use_input_video_fps", False),
    60→        "phase_config": orchestrator_payload.get("phase_config"),
    61→        "num_inference_steps": orchestrator_payload.get("num_inference_steps"),
    62→        "guidance_scale": orchestrator_payload.get("guidance_scale"),
    63→        "seed": orchestrator_payload.get("seed", -1),
    64→        # LoRA parameters
    65→        "additional_loras": orchestrator_payload.get("additional_loras", {}),
    66→        # Keep bridging image param
    67→        "keep_bridging_images": orchestrator_payload.get("keep_bridging_images", False),
    68→        # Vid2vid initialization for replace mode
    69→        "vid2vid_init_strength": orchestrator_payload.get("vid2vid_init_strength"),
    70→        # Audio to add to final output (only used by last join)
    71→        "audio_url": orchestrator_payload.get("audio_url"),
    72→    }

    74→
    75→def _check_existing_join_tasks(
    76→    orchestrator_task_id_str: str,
    77→    num_joins: int,
    78→    **_kwargs
    79→) -> Tuple[Optional[bool], Optional[str]]:
    80→    """
    81→    Check for existing child tasks (idempotency check).
    82→
    83→    Handles both patterns:
    84→    - Chain pattern: num_joins join_clips_segment tasks
    85→    - Parallel pattern: num_joins join_clips_segment (transitions) + 1 join_final_stitch
    86→
    87→    Returns:
    88→        (None, None) if no existing tasks or should proceed with creation
    89→        (success: bool, message: str) if should return early (complete/failed/in-progress)
    90→    """
    91→    task_logger.debug(f"[JOIN_CORE] Checking for existing child tasks", task_id=orchestrator_task_id_str)
    92→    existing_child_tasks = db_ops.get_orchestrator_child_tasks(orchestrator_task_id_str)
    93→    existing_joins = existing_child_tasks.get('join_clips_segment', [])
    94→    existing_final_stitch = existing_child_tasks.get('join_final_stitch', [])
    95→
    96→    # Determine which pattern was used
    97→    is_parallel_pattern = len(existing_final_stitch) > 0
    98→
    99→    if not existing_joins and not existing_final_stitch:
   100→        return None, None
   101→
   102→    task_logger.debug(f"[JOIN_CORE] Found {len(existing_joins)} join tasks, {len(existing_final_stitch)} final stitch tasks", task_id=orchestrator_task_id_str)
   103→
   104→    # Check completion status helper
   105→    def is_complete(task):
   106→        return (task.get('status', '') or '').lower() == 'complete'
   107→
   108→    def is_terminal_failure(task):
   109→        status = task.get('status', '').lower()
   110→        return status in ('failed', 'cancelled', 'canceled', 'error')
   111→
   112→    if is_parallel_pattern:
   113→        # === PARALLEL PATTERN ===
   114→        if len(existing_joins) < num_joins:
   115→            return None, None
   116→
   117→        all_tasks = existing_joins + existing_final_stitch
   118→        any_failed = any(is_terminal_failure(t) for t in all_tasks)
   119→
   120→        if any_failed:
   121→            failed_tasks = [t for t in all_tasks if is_terminal_failure(t)]
   122→            error_msg = f"{len(failed_tasks)} task(s) failed/cancelled"
   123→            task_logger.debug(f"[JOIN_CORE] FAILED: {error_msg}", task_id=orchestrator_task_id_str)
   124→            return False, f"[ORCHESTRATOR_FAILED] {error_msg}"
   125→
   126→        if existing_final_stitch and is_complete(existing_final_stitch[0]):
   127→            final_stitch = existing_final_stitch[0]
   128→            final_output = final_stitch.get('output_location', 'Completed via idempotency')
   129→            task_logger.debug(f"[JOIN_CORE] COMPLETE (parallel): Final stitch done, output: {final_output}", task_id=orchestrator_task_id_str)
   130→            completion_data = json.dumps({"output_location": final_output, "thumbnail_url": ""})
   131→            return True, f"[ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE]{completion_data}"
   132→
   133→        trans_complete = sum(1 for j in existing_joins if is_complete(j))
   134→        stitch_status = "complete" if existing_final_stitch and is_complete(existing_final_stitch[0]) else "pending"
   135→        task_logger.debug(f"[JOIN_CORE] IDEMPOTENT (parallel): {trans_complete}/{num_joins} transitions, stitch: {stitch_status}", task_id=orchestrator_task_id_str)
   136→        return True, f"[IDEMPOTENT] Parallel: {trans_complete}/{num_joins} transitions complete, stitch: {stitch_status}"
   137→
   138→    else:
   139→        # === CHAIN PATTERN (legacy) ===
   140→        if len(existing_joins) < num_joins:
   141→            return None, None
   142→
   143→        task_logger.debug(f"[JOIN_CORE] All {num_joins} join tasks already exist (chain pattern)", task_id=orchestrator_task_id_str)
   144→
   145→        all_joins_complete = all(is_complete(join) for join in existing_joins)
   146→        any_join_failed = any(is_terminal_failure(join) for join in existing_joins)
   147→
   148→        if any_join_failed:
   149→            failed_joins = [j for j in existing_joins if is_terminal_failure(j)]
   150→            error_msg = f"{len(failed_joins)} join task(s) failed/cancelled"
   151→            task_logger.debug(f"[JOIN_CORE] FAILED: {error_msg}", task_id=orchestrator_task_id_str)
   152→            return False, f"[ORCHESTRATOR_FAILED] {error_msg}"
   153→
   154→        if all_joins_complete:
   155→            def get_join_index(task):
   156→                params = task.get('task_params', {})
   157→                if isinstance(params, str):
   158→                    try:
   159→                        params = json.loads(params)
   160→                    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
   161→                        return 0
   162→                return params.get('join_index', 0)
   163→
   164→            sorted_joins = sorted(existing_joins, key=get_join_index)
   165→            final_join = sorted_joins[-1]
   166→            final_output = final_join.get('output_location', 'Completed via idempotency')
   167→
   168→            final_params = final_join.get('task_params', {})
   169→            if isinstance(final_params, str):
   170→                try:
   171→                    final_params = json.loads(final_params)
   172→                except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
   173→                    final_params = {}
   174→
   175→            final_thumbnail = final_params.get('thumbnail_url', '')
   176→
   177→            task_logger.debug(f"[JOIN_CORE] COMPLETE: All joins finished, final output: {final_output}", task_id=orchestrator_task_id_str)
   178→            completion_data = json.dumps({"output_location": final_output, "thumbnail_url": final_thumbnail})
   179→            return True, f"[ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE]{completion_data}"
   180→
   181→        complete_count = sum(1 for j in existing_joins if is_complete(j))
   182→        task_logger.debug(f"[JOIN_CORE] IDEMPOTENT: {complete_count}/{num_joins} joins complete", task_id=orchestrator_task_id_str)
   183→        return True, f"[IDEMPOTENT] Join tasks in progress: {complete_count}/{num_joins} complete"
```

## TaskRegistry.dispatch() and Handler Function Signatures - Context Dict Contract Analysis

### 1. **TaskRegistry.dispatch() Method (task_registry.py:1082-1195)**

The `dispatch()` method accepts a **context** dictionary with the following keys:

```python
context = {
    "task_params_dict": dict,           # Task parameters from DB
    "main_output_dir_base": Path,       # Base output directory
    "task_id": str,                     # Unique task ID
    "project_id": str | None,           # Project ID (orchestrator tasks)
    "task_queue": HeadlessTaskQueue,    # Task queue instance
    "colour_match_videos": bool,        # Color matching flag
    "mask_active_frames": bool,         # Mask active frames flag
    "debug_mode": bool,                 # Debug flag
    "wan2gp_path": str,                 # Path to Wan2GP directory
}
```

**Source:** Lines 136-146 in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Headless-Wan2GP/worker.py` where context is constructed in `process_single_task()`.

### 2. **Handler Function Signatures - The "Different Contract Per Handler" Pattern**

The registry DOES NOT pass a single unified `context` dict to all handlers. Instead, each handler type receives **a different set of parameters extracted from context**:

### 3. **Handler Registration in dispatch() (task_registry.py:1110-1189)**

The handlers are registered as lambdas that destructure context keys:

```python

    "travel_orchestrator": lambda: travel_orchestrator.handle_travel_orchestrator_task(
        task_params_from_db=params,
        main_output_dir_base=context["main_output_dir_base"],
```

### 4. **Task Params Dict Keys Accessed by Handlers**

Handlers read different keys from `task_params_dict` / `task_params_from_db`:

| Handler | Keys Accessed |

| **extract_frame.py** | `input_video_task_id`, `frame_index`, `output_dir` |
| **rife_interpolate.py** | `input_image_path1`, `input_image_path2`, `output_path`, `frames`, `resolution`, `output_dir` |
| **magic_edit.py** | (checks for `replicate` availability, then uses orchestrator_details) |
| **inpaint_frames.py** | `video_path`, `inpaint_start_frame`, `inpaint_end_frame`, `context_frame_count`, `prompt`, `model` |
| **travel/orchestrator.py** | `orchestrator_details` (nested dict with extensive schema) |
| **travel_segment_via_queue** | Complex hierarchical resolution: `orchestrator_details`, `individual_segment_params`, `segment_params`, etc. (lines 121-560) |
| **join/orchestrator.py** | `orchestrator_details` (nested dict) |

### 5. **Key Findings**

1. **No Unified Context Contract**: The `dispatch()` method extracts different subsets from `context` for each handler type. There is no single "context" dict passed to all handlers.

2. **Parameter Naming Inconsistency**:
   - Some handlers use `task_params_dict`, others use `task_params_from_db`
   - Some handlers use `task_id`, others use `orchestrator_task_id_str` or `stitch_task_id_str`
   - This inconsistency is hardcoded in the lambda registrations (lines 1110-1180)

3. **Task Queue Integration**:
   - **Not all handlers receive `task_queue`**: Only travel_segment, rife_interpolate, join_clips_segment, and inpaint_frames get it
   - Orchestrators do NOT receive `task_queue` (they create child tasks instead)
   - Direct queue tasks (extract_frame, magic_edit, comfy) do NOT receive `task_queue`

4. **Debug Mode and WGP Path**:
   - **Neither `debug_mode` nor `wan2gp_path` are passed to any handler**
   - These are constructed in `context` but never used by `dispatch()` or any handler function
   - This appears to be **dead data in the context dict**

5. **Orchestrator Pattern**:
   - Travel orchestrators receive `orchestrator_project_id`
   - Other handlers do NOT receive project_id
   - Orchestrators receive the base context but skip task_queue/colour_match/mask flags

### 6. **Handler Parameter Extraction Patterns**

Lines 1102-1103 show the core extraction:
```python
task_id = context["task_id"]
params = context["task_params_dict"]
```

Then each handler is called with custom subsets via lambdas (1110-1180).

---

## Summary

**The "context" dict contract is NOT unified**. Instead:

1. `dispatch()` receives a 8-key context dict
2. It extracts 2 keys immediately: `task_id` and `task_params_dict`
3. For each handler type, it creates a lambda that passes **different subsets** of context to the handler
4. Most handlers receive only 3-4 parameters (not the full context)
5. **`debug_mode` and `wan2gp_path` are unused** and should be removed from context construction
6. Handler signatures vary significantly with no clear contract or TypedDict defining expected parameters

This is the architectural issue that Phase 4 (TypedDict contracts) should address.

## CRITICAL NOTES

1. **Dual naming support**: `orchestrator_details` is the canonical key name, but `full_orchestrator_payload` is used as a legacy alias in travel/stitch.py and travel/chaining.py
2. **Mutated during orchestration**: Several keys (segment_frames_expanded, frame_overlap_expanded, parsed_resolution_wh, etc.) are modified/optimized during orchestration execution
3. **Internal keys**: Keys prefixed with `_` (like `_consolidated_end_anchors`, `_consolidated_keyframe_positions`) are internal optimization data set during orchestration
4. **Nested dicts**: `original_task_args`, `original_common_args`, and nested `orchestrator_details` exist for compatibility/traceability
5. **Travel vs Join separation**: Travel orchestrator focuses on generation parameters; join orchestrator focuses on clip transitions
6. **Structure guidance**: All structure video keys are optional and only used when structure guidance is enabled

```
   358→
   359→            if not task_info:
   360→                time.sleep(cli_args.poll_interval)
   361→                continue
   362→
   363→            current_task_params = task_info["params"]
   364→            current_task_type = task_info["task_type"]
   365→            current_project_id = task_info.get("project_id")
   366→            current_task_id = task_info["task_id"]
   367→
   368→            if current_project_id is None and current_task_type in {"travel_orchestrator", "edit_video_orchestrator"}:

   382→            task_succeeded, output_location = process_single_task(

   394→

   404→                        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, KeyError):

   407→                        db_ops.update_task_status_supabase(current_task_id, db_ops.STATUS_COMPLETE, actual_output, thumbnail_url)
   408→                    else:

   410→                else:

   412→

   416→                    cleanup_generated_files(output_location, current_task_id, debug_mode)
   417→            else:
   418→                # Task failed - check if this is a retryable error
   419→                error_message = output_location or "Unknown error"

   421→                current_attempts = task_info.get("attempts", 0)

   423→                if is_retryable and current_attempts < max_attempts:
   424→                    # Requeue for retry

   429→                    db_ops.requeue_task_for_retry(

   435→                else:

   440→                        )
   441→                    db_ops.update_task_status_supabase(current_task_id, db_ops.STATUS_FAILED, output_location)
   442→            
   443→            # Clear task context from log interceptor
```

```
   101→def _get_param(key, *sources, default=_MISSING, prefer_truthy: bool = False):
   102→    """
   103→    Get a parameter from multiple sources with precedence (first source wins).
   104→
   105→    By default, only skips None values.
   106→    If prefer_truthy=True, also skips falsy non-bool values (e.g. "", {}, [], 0),
   107→    matching historical `a or b` fallback semantics while still preserving explicit booleans.
   108→    """
   109→    for source in sources:
   110→        if not source or key not in source:
   111→            continue
   112→
   113→        value = source[key]
   114→        if value is None:
   115→            continue
   116→
   117→        if prefer_truthy and not isinstance(value, bool) and not value:
   118→            continue
   119→
   120→        return value
   121→
   122→    return None if default is _MISSING else default
   123→
   124→def _resolve_segment_context(task_params_dict: dict, is_standalone: bool, task_id: str) -> SegmentContext:
   125→    """Resolve mode, orchestrator_details, individual_params, and segment identity.
   126→
   127→    Handles orchestrator vs standalone mode, fetching orchestrator_details from the DB
   128→    if not provided inline.
   129→
   130→    Raises ValueError if required fields are missing.
   131→    """

   133→    orchestrator_task_id_ref = segment_params.get("orchestrator_task_id_ref")
   134→    orchestrator_run_id = segment_params.get("orchestrator_run_id")
   135→    segment_idx = segment_params.get("segment_index")
   136→
   137→    # Get orchestrator_details (canonical name) or full_orchestrator_payload (legacy alias)
   138→    orchestrator_details: dict = segment_params.get("orchestrator_details") or segment_params.get("full_orchestrator_payload")
   139→
   140→    if is_standalone:
   141→        # Standalone mode: use provided payload, default segment_idx to 0
   142→        if segment_idx is None:
   143→            segment_idx = 0
   144→        if not orchestrator_details:
   145→            raise ValueError(f"Individual travel segment {task_id} missing orchestrator_details")
   146→        headless_logger.debug(f"Running in standalone mode (individual_travel_segment)", task_id=task_id)
   147→    else:
   148→        # Orchestrator mode: require segment_index and either inline orchestrator_details or ability to fetch
   149→        if segment_idx is None:
   150→            raise ValueError(f"Travel segment {task_id} missing segment_index")
   151→
   152→        # If orchestrator_details not inline, try to fetch from parent task
   153→        if not orchestrator_details:
   154→            if not orchestrator_task_id_ref:

   161→        if not orchestrator_details:
   162→            raise ValueError(f"Travel segment {task_id}: Could not retrieve orchestrator_details")
   163→
   164→    # individual_segment_params has highest priority for segment-specific overrides
   165→    individual_params: IndividualSegmentParams = segment_params.get("individual_segment_params", {})
```
